q: By the oath of those angels who stand in rows
(engaged in Ibaadah or awaiting instructions from Allaah)!
v.s: By those [angels] lined up in rows
v.c: By those ˹angels˺ lined up in ranks,

v.s: And those who drive [the clouds]
v.c: and those who diligently drive ˹the clouds˺,

q: And by those angels who recite the 'Reminder'
v.s: And those who recite the message,
v.c: and those who recite the Reminder!

q: Without doubt, your Ilaah is One.
v.s: Indeed, your God is One,
v.c: Surely your God is One!

q: He is the Rabb of the heavens, the earth, whatever is between the two and He is the Rabb of the points of the sun's rising
(the various points on the eastern horizon from which the sun rises during the different seasons).
v.s: Lord of the heavens and the earth and that between them and Lord of the sunrises.
v.c: ˹He is˺ the Lord of the heavens and the earth and everything in between, and the Lord of all points of sunrise.

q: the sky of this world with the adornment
v.s: Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment of stars
v.c: Indeed, We have adorned the lowest heaven with the stars for decoration

q: ...as a protection from every rebellious Shaytaan.
v.s: And as protection against every rebellious devil
v.c: and ˹for˺ protection from every rebellious devil.

v.s: [So] they may not listen to the exalted assembly [of angels] and are pelted from every side,
v.c: They cannot listen to the highest assembly ˹of angels˺ for they are pelted from every side,

v.s: Repelled; and for them is a constant punishment,
v.c: ˹fiercely˺ driven away. And they will suffer an everlasting torment.

q: Except for the one who snatches

(and destroys him). (However, some of them manage to quickly pass on the information to other Shayaateen before dying and pass the incorrect information mixed with his goes on to the fortune tellers on earth.)
v.s: Except one who snatches [some words] by theft, but they are pursued by a burning flame, piercing [in brightness].
v.c: But whoever manages to stealthily eavesdrop is ˹instantly˺ pursued by a piercing flare.

q: (If the Kuffaar claim that We cannot resurrect people on the Day of Qiyaamah,)
Ask them whether their creating them was more difficult than the other things We created.
(When We were able to create great creations, bringing man back will be extremely simple).
(which is a weak, pliable substance compared to what Allaah used to create His other creation).
v.s: Then inquire of them, [O Muhammad], “Are they a stronger [or more difficult] creation or those [others] We have created?” Indeed, We created them [i.e., men] from sticky clay.
v.c: So ask them ˹O Prophet˺, which is harder to create: them or other marvels of Our creation? Indeed, We created them from a sticky clay.

q: (Islaam and the Qur'aan when they have no cause to do so).
v.s: But you wonder, while they mock,
v.c: In fact, you are astonished ˹by their denial˺, while they ridicule ˹you˺.

v.s: And when they are reminded, they remember not.
v.c: When they are reminded, they are never mindful.

q: (to prove the Prophethood of a Nabi),
v.s: And when they see a sign, they ridicule.
v.c: And whenever they see a sign, they make fun of it,

v.s: And say, "This is not but obvious magic.
v.c: saying, “This is nothing but pure magic.

q: after we have died and become dust and bones?”
v.s: When we have died and become dust and bones, are we indeed to be resurrected?
v.c: When we are dead and reduced to dust and bones, will we really be resurrected?

v.s: And our forefathers [as well]?"
v.c: And our forefathers as well?”

q: Say, “Yes! And you will be disgraced
(when you learn that you had been foolish to reject resurrection).”
v.s: Say, "Yes, and you will be [rendered] contemptible."
v.c: Say, “Yes! And you will be fully humbled.”

q: There will be only a single shout
(blast of the trumpet to announce the arrival of Qiyaamah),
after which they will all instantly stand up
v.s: It will be only one shout, and at once they will be observing.
v.c: It will only take one Blast, then at once they will see ˹it all˺.

q: They will say, “Alas! This is the Day of Reckoning
v.s: They will say, "O woe to us! This is the Day of Recompense."
v.c: They will cry, “Oh, woe to us! This is the Day of Judgment!”

q: Day which you used to deny.”
v.s: [They will be told], "This is the Day of Judgement which you used to deny."
v.c: ˹They will be told,˺ “This is the Day of ˹Final˺ Decision which you used to deny.”

q: (The angels will then be commanded to)
v.s: [The angels will be ordered], "Gather those who committed wrong, their kinds, and what they used to worship
v.c: ˹Allah will say to the angels,˺ “Gather ˹all˺ the wrongdoers along with their peers, and whatever they used to worship

q: “...apart from Allaah, and lead them to the road of the Blaze
v.s: Other than God, and guide them to the path of Hellfire
v.c: instead of Allah, then lead them ˹all˺ to the path of Hell.

q: Stop them, for they will have to be questioned.”
v.s: And stop them; indeed, they are to be questioned."
v.c: And detain them, for they must be questioned.”

q: with you that you do not help each other
(whereas you promised each other that your gods will assist you and that you would assist each other)?”
v.s: [They will be asked], "What is [wrong] with you? Why do you not help each other?"
v.c: ˹Then they will be asked,˺ “What is the matter with you that you can no longer help each other?”

q: On that day they will have submit
(to the judgment because everything will be apparent before them and they will be unable to deny anything).
v.s: But they, that Day, are in surrender.
v.c: In fact, on that Day they will be ˹fully˺ submissive.

q: They will turn to each other asking questions.
v.s: And they will approach one another asking [i.e., blaming] each other.
v.c: They will turn on each other, throwing blame.

q: “You people used to come to us with great might
v.s: They will say, "Indeed, you used to come at us from the right."
v.c: The misled will say, “It was you who deluded us away from what is right.”

q: The leaders will reply, “But you people were never Mu'mineen
(in the first place, so you cannot claim that we took you away from Islaam).”
v.s: They [i.e., the oppressors] will say, "Rather, you [yourselves] were not believers,
v.c: The misleaders will reply, “No! You disbelieved on your own.

q: “We never had any authority over you
(and could therefore not compel you to remain as Kuffaar).
However, you were a rebellious nation
(exceeding the limits and would have remained Kuffaar even if we told you nothing).'
v.s: And we had over you no authority, but you were a transgressing people.
v.c: We had no authority over you. In fact, you yourselves were a transgressing people.

q: “(Nevertheless, it is too late to alter our fate because)
against us. Undoubtedly, we shall all taste
v.s: So the word [i.e., decree] of our Lord has come into effect upon us; indeed, we will taste [punishment].
v.c: The decree of our Lord has come to pass against us ˹all˺: we will certainly taste ˹the punishment˺.

q: (The Kuffaar leaders will further tell their followers)
(only because you were prepared to listen to us)
(not guided by our own choice. Therefore, neither you or we can blame anyone).'
v.s: And we led you to deviation; indeed, we were deviators."
v.c: We caused you to deviate, for we ourselves were deviant.”

q: Undoubtedly, they will all share in the punishment
v.s: So indeed they, that Day, will be sharing in the punishment.
v.c: Surely on that Day they will ˹all˺ share in the punishment.

q: Thus do We treat the criminals
v.s: Indeed, that is how We deal with the criminals.
v.c: That is certainly how We deal with the wicked.

q: They were the ones who were
when they were told, “There is none worthy of worship but Allaah.”
v.s: Indeed they, when it was said to them, "There is no deity but God," were arrogant
v.c: For whenever it was said to them ˹in the world˺, “There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Allah,” they acted arrogantly

q: They used to say, “Should we leave our gods for an insane
v.s: And were saying, "Are we to leave our gods for a mad poet?"
v.c: and argued, “Should we really abandon our gods for a mad poet?”

q: and he ﷺ confirms the Ambiyaa ﵊
(who had informed their people about his arrival).
v.s: Rather, he [i.e., the Prophet (ﷺ)] has come with the truth and confirmed the [previous] messengers.
v.c: In fact, he came with the truth, confirming ˹earlier˺ messengers.

q: “You will all definitely taste a grievous
v.s: Indeed, you [disbelievers] will be tasters of the painful punishment,
v.c: You will certainly taste the painful torment,

q: “You will be punished only for the actions that you carried out
(and not for anything you did not do).”
v.s: And you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do -
v.c: and will only be rewarded for what you used to do.

q: Of course, the situation of Allaah's selected bondsmen
v.s: But not the chosen servants of God.
v.c: But not the chosen servants of Allah.

q: For these people there will be a familiar provision...
v.s: Those will have a provision determined -
v.c: They will have a known provision:

q: (fruit that they will recognise but which will be far superior to the fruit of this world).
v.s: Fruits; and they will be honoured
v.c: fruits ˹of every type˺. And they will be honoured

v.s: In gardens of pleasure
v.c: in the Gardens of Bliss,

v.s: On thrones facing one another.
v.c: facing each other on thrones.

q: They will be presented with goblets
(unlike the impure wine of this world which intoxicates)...
v.s: There will be circulated among them a cup [of wine] from a flowing spring,
v.c: A drink ˹of pure wine˺ will be passed around to them from a flowing stream:

v.s: White and delicious to the drinkers;
v.c: crystal-white, delicious to drink.

q: nor will they be intoxicated by it.
v.s: No bad effect is there in it, nor from it will they be intoxicated.
v.c: It will neither harm ˹them˺, nor will they be intoxicated by it.

v.s: And with them will be women limiting [their] glances, with large, [beautiful] eyes,
v.c: And with them will be maidens of modest gaze and gorgeous eyes,

q: (Their skin tone will be so clear that it will appear)
v.s: As if they were [delicate] eggs, well-protected.
v.c: as if they were pristine pearls.

q: will face each other, questioning each other.
v.s: And they will approach one another, inquiring of each other.
v.c: Then they will turn to one another inquisitively.

q: One of them will say, “I had a certain companion
(friend who did not believe in resurrection)...”
v.s: A speaker among them will say, "Indeed, I had a companion [on earth].
v.c: One of them will say, “I once had a companion ˹in the world˺

q: “...who used to say, 'Are you from those who confirm
v.s: Who would say, 'Are you indeed of those who believe
v.c: who used to ask ˹me˺, ‘Do you actually believe ˹in resurrection˺?

q: 'Will we really be given the retribution
when we die and become sand and bones?”'
v.s: That when we have died and become dust and bones, we will indeed be recompensed?'"
v.c: When we are dead and reduced to dust and bones, will we really be brought to judgment?’”

q: “Do you want to have a look
v.s: He will say, "Would you [care to] look?"
v.c: He will ˹then˺ ask, “Would you care to see ˹his fate˺?”

v.s: And he will look and see him in the midst of the Hellfire.
v.c: Then he ˹and the others˺ will look and spot him in the midst of the Hellfire.

q: will say, “By Allaah! You almost destroyed me
v.s: He will say, "By God, you almost ruined me.
v.c: He will ˹then˺ say, “By Allah! You nearly ruined me.

q: “If it were not for the bounty of my Rabb
I would have certainly been from those brought forward
v.s: If not for the favor of my Lord, I would have been of those brought in [to Hell].
v.c: Had it not been for the grace of my Lord, I ˹too˺ would have certainly been among those brought ˹to Hell˺.”

q: “Is it not so that we shall not die again
v.s: Then, are we not to die
v.c: ˹Then he will ask his fellow believers,˺ “Can you imagine that we will never die,

q: (which already took place in the world),
and we will not be punished?”
v.s: Except for our first death, and we will not be punished?"
v.c: except our first death, nor be punished ˹like the others˺?”

v.s: Indeed, this is the great attainment.
v.c: This is truly the ultimate triumph.

q: that those who wish to strive should strive
v.s: For the like of this let the workers [on earth] work.
v.c: For such ˹honour˺ all should strive.

q: better hospitality or the tree of Zaqqoom?
v.s: Is that [i.e., Paradise] a better accommodation or the tree of zaqqūm?
v.c: Is this ˹bliss˺ a better accommodation or the tree of Zaqqûm?
v.h: Hospitality for the People of Hell

q: (the Kuffaar who mocked Rasulullaah ﷺ by saying that a tree cannot grow in the fire of Jahannam).
v.s: Indeed, We have made it a torment for the wrongdoers.
v.c: We have surely made it a test for the wrongdoers.

q: is a tree that emerges from the depths of Jahannam.
v.s: Indeed, it is a tree issuing from the bottom of the Hellfire,
v.c: Indeed, it is a tree that grows in the depths of Hell,

v.s: Its emerging fruit as if it was heads of the devils.
v.c: bearing fruit like devils’ heads.

q: People will certainly eat from it and
(although it will taste horrible, they will)
v.s: And indeed, they will eat from it and fill with it their bellies.
v.c: The evildoers will certainly ˹be left to˺ eat from it, filling up their bellies with it.

q: they will be given a mixture of boiling water with it
(which will be so hot that it will burn their entrails to shreds).
v.s: Then indeed, they will have after it a mixture of scalding water.
v.c: Then on top of that they will be given a blend of boiling drink.

q: their return will definitely be towards the blazing fire
(of Jahannam, where the punishment will resume).
v.s: Then indeed, their return will be to the Hellfire.
v.c: Then they will ultimately return to ˹their place in˺ Hell.

v.s: Indeed they found their fathers astray.
v.c: Indeed, they found their forefathers astray,

v.s: So they hastened [to follow] in their footsteps.
v.c: so they rushed in their footsteps!

v.s: And there had already strayed before them most of the former peoples,
v.c: And surely most of the earlier generations had strayed before them,

q: (However, We did not leave them to their own devices, but)
We certainly sent warners among them
(to warn them about the consequences of kufr).
v.s: And We had already sent among them warners.
v.c: although We had certainly sent warners among them.

q: (However, they rejected the reminders and were soon destroyed by Allaah's punishment.)
(but who did not heed the warning).
v.s: Then look how was the end of those who were warned -
v.c: See then what was the end of those who had been warned.

q: Of course, the situation of Allaah's chosen bondsmen
(they accepted the message of the Ambiyaa ﵊ and attained success in the Aakhirah).
v.s: But not the chosen servants of God.
v.c: But not the chosen servants of Allah.

q: (to save him from his people). (We accepted his du'aa and sent a flood to destroy them.)
(answer to the one who pleads for help)?
v.s: And Noah had certainly called Us, and [We are] the best of responders.
v.c: Indeed, Noah cried out to Us, and how excellent are We in responding!

q: We rescued him and his family from a great calamity
(the flood, while all the Kuffaar were drowned).
v.s: And We saved him and his family from the great affliction.
v.c: We delivered him and his family from the great distress,

v.s: And We made his descendants those remaining [on the earth]
v.c: and made his descendants the sole survivors.

q: And, in his favour, We left
among those to come after him...
v.s: And left for him [favorable mention] among later generations:
v.c: And We blessed him ˹with honourable mention˺ among later generations:

q: ...“Peace be to Nooh ﵊ in the universe.”
(He is therefore remembered with words like this by all Mu'mineen.)
v.s: "Peace upon Noah among the worlds."
v.c: “Peace be upon Noah among all peoples.”

q: Thus do We reward those who do good.
v.s: Indeed, We thus reward the doers of good.
v.c: Indeed, this is how We reward the good-doers.

q: was certainly from Our slaves who were Mu'mineen.
v.s: Indeed, he was of Our believing servants.
v.c: ˹For˺ he was truly one of Our faithful servants.

v.s: Then We drowned the others [i.e., disbelievers].
v.c: Then We drowned the others.

v.s: And indeed, among his kind was Abraham,
v.c: And indeed, one of those who followed his way was Abraham.

q: came to his Rabb with a sound
(that was free from Shirk and sin).
v.s: When he came to his Lord with a sound heart
v.c: ˹Remember˺ when he came to his Lord with a pure heart,

q: when he said to his people and his father, “What do you worship?”
v.s: [And] when he said to his father and his people, "What do you worship?
v.c: and said to his father and his people, “What are you worshipping?

v.s: Is it falsehood [as] gods other than God you desire?
v.c: Is it false gods that you desire instead of Allah?

q: “What is your opinion about the Rabb of the universe?”
(Do you think that He will leave you to worship these idols without being punished?)
v.s: Then what is your thought about the Lord of the worlds?"
v.c: What then do you expect from the Lord of all worlds?”

q: (Once, when the people of Ibraheem ﵊ prepared to leave town for a celebration, they asked him to accompany them. In reply)
He glanced once at the stars
v.s: And he cast a look at the stars.
v.c: He later looked up to the stars ˹in contemplation˺,

q: (Because they believed that the stars had an effect on people, they did not question his illness.)
v.s: And said, "Indeed, I am [about to be] ill."
v.c: then said, “I am really sick.”

q: So they turned their backs on him and left.
v.s: So they turned away from him, departing.
v.c: So they turned their backs on him and went away.

q: (seeing all the food that the people had left as offering, he)
v.s: Then he turned to their gods and said, "Do you not eat?
v.c: Then he ˹stealthily˺ advanced towards their gods, and said ˹mockingly˺, “Will you not eat ˹your offerings˺?

q: “What is the matter with you that you do not speak?”
v.s: What is [wrong] with you that you do not speak?".
v.c: What is wrong with you that you cannot speak?”

q: He then turned to them, striking them with force
(with the right hand breaking all of them except the largest one whom he left untouched). (As mentioned in verses 59-61 of Surah 21, the people learnt that Ibraheem ﵊ was responsible for the act.)
v.s: And he turned upon them a blow with [his] right hand.
v.c: Then he swiftly turned on them, striking ˹them˺ with his right hand.

q: The people came to him in haste
(extremely upset to question him about the incident).
v.s: Then they [i.e., the people] came toward him, hastening.
v.c: Later, his people came rushing towards him ˹furiously˺.

q: (Seizing the opportunity to make them understand the folly of worshipping idols,)
He said, “Do you worship what you yourselves carve...”
v.s: He said, "Do you worship that which you [yourselves] carve,
v.c: He argued, “How can you worship what you carve ˹with your own hands˺,

q: “...whereas Allaah has created you and anything that you make?”
(Why do you worship the creation instead of The Creator?)
v.s: While God created you and that which you do?"
v.c: when it is Allah Who created you and whatever you do?”

q: said, “Construct a building for him and cast him into a blazing fire.”
v.s: They said, "Construct for him a structure [i.e., furnace] and throw him into the burning fire."
v.c: They said ˹to one another˺, “Build him a furnace and cast him into the blazing fire.”

q: They devised a plot against him, but We made them the ones to look down
(in humility when their plan to kill him failed. See verses 68-70 of Surah 21).
v.s: And they intended for him a plan [i.e., harm], but We made them the most debased.
v.c: And so they sought to harm him, but We made them inferior.

q: (When his father and his people refused to accept his message of Towheed)
(has commanded me to go), (it is only Allaah)
(to the blessed land of Shaam, where I am commanded to live).”
v.s: And [then] he said, "Indeed, I will go to [where I am ordered by] my Lord; He will guide me.
v.c: He later said, “I am leaving ˹in obedience˺ to my Lord. He will guide me.

q: “O my Rabb! Grant me a son
v.s: My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous."
v.c: My Lord! Bless me with righteous offspring.”

m: So We gave him the glad tidings
q: So We conveyed to him the good news of
v.s: So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy.
v.c: So We gave him good news of a forbearing son.

q: reached the age where he could run about, he
said to him, “O my beloved son! Verily, I have seen
in a dream that I am slaughtering you. So
(on the matter because your life is at stake).”
replied, “O my beloved father! Do as you have been commanded
(because the dreams of the Ambiyaa are revelation).
If Allaah wills, you will soon find me to be among the patient ones
v.s: And when he reached with him [the age of] exertion, he said, "O my son, indeed I have seen in a dream that I [must] sacrifice you, so see what you think." He said, "O my father, do as you are commanded. You will find me, if God wills, of the steadfast."
v.c: Then when the boy reached the age to work with him, Abraham said, “O my dear son! I have seen in a dream that I ˹must˺ sacrifice you. So tell me what you think.” He replied, “O my dear father! Do as you are commanded. Allah willing, you will find me steadfast.”

q: (to Allaah's command, they proceeded to carry out the sacrifice)
turned his son on his side
(to slaughter him, placing the knife on the youth's throat)...
v.s: And when they had both submitted and he put him down upon his forehead,
v.c: Then when they submitted ˹to Allah’s Will˺, and Abraham laid him on the side of his forehead ˹for sacrifice˺,

m: And We called out to him
q: (stopped him from slaughtering his son and)
v.s: We called to him, "O Abraham,
v.c: We called out to him, “O Abraham!

q: “You have certainly brought the dream to a realisation
do We reward those who do good.”
v.s: You have fulfilled the vision." Indeed, We thus reward the doers of good.
v.c: You have already fulfilled the vision.” Indeed, this is how We reward the good-doers.

v.s: Indeed, this was the clear trial.
v.c: That was truly a revealing test.

q: (a ram from Jannah, which Ibraheem ﵊ then slaughtered in the place of Ismaa'eel
v.s: And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice,
v.c: And We ransomed his son with a great sacrifice,

q: And, in his favour, We left
among those to come after him...
v.s: And We left for him [favorable mention] among later generations:
v.c: and blessed Abraham ˹with honourable mention˺ among later generations:

q: (He is therefore remembered with words like this by all Mu'mineen.)
v.s: "Peace upon Abraham."
v.c: “Peace be upon Abraham.”

q: Thus do We reward those who do good.
v.s: Indeed, We thus reward the doers of good.
v.c: This is how We reward the good-doers.

q: He was certainly from Our slaves
v.s: Indeed, he was of Our believing servants.
v.c: He was truly one of Our faithful servants.

m: And We gave him glad tidings
q: We gave him the good news of
v.s: And We gave him good tidings of Isaac, a prophet from among the righteous.
v.c: We ˹later˺ gave him good news of Isaac—a prophet, and one of the righteous.

q: (with numerous favours such as Prophethood, knowledge and wisdom).
of the two, there was the one who did good
as well as the open oppressor of his soul
v.s: And We blessed him and Isaac. But among their descendants is the doer of good and the clearly unjust to himself [i.e., sinner].
v.c: We blessed him and Isaac as well. Some of their descendants did good, while others clearly wronged themselves.

q: Undoubtedly We favoured Moosa ﵊ and Haaroon ﵊
v.s: And We did certainly confer favor upon Moses and Aaron.
v.c: And We certainly showed favour to Moses and Aaron,

m: And We saved both of them
q: We rescued the two of them and their people from great distress
v.s: And We saved them and their people from the great affliction,
v.c: and delivered them and their people from the great distress.

q: (surviving after Fir'oun and his army had been drowned).
v.s: And We supported them so it was they who overcame.
v.c: We helped them so it was they who prevailed.

m: And We gave both of them
q: We gave the two of them a Book
v.s: And We gave them the explicit Scripture [i.e., the Torah],
v.c: We gave them the clear Scripture,

m: And We guided both of them
q: And We guided the two of them to the straight path.
v.s: And We guided them on the straight path.
v.c: and guided them to the Straight Path.

q: And, in their favour, We left
v.s: And We left for them [favorable mention] among later generations:
v.c: And We blessed them ˹with honourable mention˺ among later generations:

q: (They are therefore remembered with words like this by all Mu'mineen.)
v.s: "Peace upon Moses and Aaron."
v.c: “Peace be upon Moses and Aaron.”

q: Thus do We reward those who do good.
v.s: Indeed, We thus reward the doers of good.
v.c: Indeed, this is how We reward the good-doers.

q: They were certainly from Our slaves who were Mu'mineen
v.s: Indeed, they were of Our believing servants.
v.c: They were truly ˹two˺ of Our faithful servants.

q: Indeed Ilyaas ﵊ was from the Ambiyaa.
(Ilyaas ﵊ preached to the people of B'albak, a town in Shaam.)
v.s: And indeed, Elias was from among the messengers,
v.c: And Elias was indeed one of the messengers.

q: When he said to his people, “Do you not fear
(Allaah's punishment for worshipping others besides Him)?”
v.s: When he said to his people, "Will you not fear God?
v.c: ˹Remember˺ when he said to his people, “Will you not fear ˹Allah˺?

q: Ba'al and leave out the Best of all creators
v.s: Do you call upon Baʿl and leave the best of creators -
v.c: Do you call upon ˹the idol of˺ Ba’l and abandon the Best of Creators—

q: “Allaah is your Rabb and the Rabb of your predecessors
v.s: God, your Lord and the Lord of your first forefathers?"
v.c: Allah, your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers?”

q: They rejected him, so they will certainly be brought forward
v.s: And they denied him, so indeed, they will be brought [for punishment],
v.c: But they rejected him, so they will certainly be brought ˹for punishment˺.

q: Of course, the situation of Allaah's chosen bondsmen
(for they will enjoy pleasures in Jannah and not suffer punishment).
v.s: Except the chosen servants of God.
v.c: But not the chosen servants of Allah.

q: And, in his favour, We left
v.s: And We left for him [favorable mention] among later generations:
v.c: We blessed him ˹with honourable mention˺ among later generations:

q: (Ilyaas ﵊)” (He is therefore remembered with words like this by all Mu'mineen.))
v.s: "Peace upon Elias."
v.c: “Peace be upon Elias.”

q: Thus do We reward those who do good.
v.s: Indeed, We thus reward the doers of good.
v.c: Indeed, this is how We reward the good-doers.

q: He was certainly from Our slaves
v.s: Indeed, he was of Our believing servants.
v.c: He was truly one of Our faithful servants.

q: Indeed Loot ﵊ was from the Ambiyaa.
v.s: And indeed, Lot was among the messengers.
v.c: And Lot was indeed one of the messengers.

q: him and all the members of his family
v.s: [So mention] when We saved him and his family, all,
v.c: ˹Remember˺ when We delivered him and all of his family,

v.s: Except an old woman [i.e., his wife] among those who remained [with the evildoers].
v.c: except an old woman, who was one of the doomed.

v.s: Then We destroyed the others.
v.c: Then We ˹utterly˺ destroyed the rest.

q: (see the ruins of their cities as you travel)
v.s: And indeed, you pass by them in the morning
v.c: You ˹Meccans˺ certainly pass by their ruins day

q: (that your fate will be the same for rejecting the message of Rasulullaah ﷺ)?
v.s: And at night. Then will you not use reason?
v.c: and night. Will you not then understand?

q: Yunus ﵊ was certainly from the Ambiyaa.
v.s: And indeed, Jonah was among the messengers.
v.c: And Jonah was indeed one of the messengers.

q: (after losing hope that his people will accept Imaan)
(the town without Allaah's command and headed)
v.s: [Mention] when he ran away to the laden ship.
v.c: ˹Remember˺ when he fled to the overloaded ship.

q: (However, when the ship set sail, it was caught in stormy weather and was close to sinking. The people on board attributed this misfortune to the fact that an escaped slave was on board. It was decided that the person should be thrown overboard to save the ship. However, to decide who the person was,)
v.s: And he drew lots and was among the losers.
v.c: Then ˹to save it from sinking,˺ he drew straws ˹with other passengers˺. He lost ˹and was thrown overboard˺.

q: (for leaving the town without waiting for Allaah's command).
v.s: Then the fish swallowed him, while he was blameworthy.
v.c: Then the whale engulfed him while he was blameworthy.

q: If he were not from those who glorify Allaah....
v.s: And had he not been of those who exalt God,
v.c: Had he not ˹constantly˺ glorified ˹Allah˺,

q: ...he would have remained inside the fish until the day people are resurrected.
v.s: He would have remained inside its belly until the Day they are resurrected.
v.c: he would have certainly remained in its belly until the Day of Resurrection.

q: (However, We rescued him from the fish and)
We cast him on a barren
(after spending a long time in the fish).
v.s: But We threw him onto the open shore while he was ill.
v.c: But We cast him onto the open ˹shore˺, ˹totally˺ worn out,

q: We then caused a creeper to grow over him
(to shade him as he regained his strength).
v.s: And We caused to grow over him a gourd vine.
v.c: and caused a squash plant to grow over him.

q: to a nation of a hundred thousand or more.
v.s: And We sent him to [his people of] a hundred thousand or more.
v.c: We ˹later˺ sent him ˹back˺ to ˹his city of˺ at least one hundred thousand people,

q: accepted Imaan and We allowed them to enjoy themselves
(rather than suffer the punishment as Yunus ﵊ had wished).
v.s: And they believed, so We gave them enjoyment [of life] for a time.
v.c: who then believed ˹in him˺, so We allowed them enjoyment for a while.

v.s: So inquire of them, [O Muhammad], “Does your Lord have daughters while they have sons?
v.c: Ask them ˹O Prophet˺ if your Lord has daughters, while the pagans ˹prefer to˺ have sons.

q: (they developed the belief that the angels are Allaah's daughters because they believe that)
We created the angels as females in their presence?”
v.s: Or did We create the angels as females while they were witnesses?"
v.c: Or ˹ask them˺ if We created the angels as females right before their eyes.

q: Behold! Because of their fabricated beliefs, they will certainly say...
v.s: Unquestionably, it is out of their [invented] falsehood that they say,
v.c: Indeed, it is one of their ˹outrageous˺ fabrications to say,

q: ...“Allaah has children.” Undoubtedly, they are liars!
v.s: "God has begotten," and indeed, they are liars.
v.c: “Allah has children.” They are simply liars.

q: Has Allaah chosen daughters instead of sons?
v.s: Has He chosen daughters over sons?
v.c: Has He chosen daughters over sons?

q: What is the matter with you people? How do you decide?
(Whereas these Mushrikeen loved sons more than daughters, it is deemed offensive that they should attribute to Allaah what they dislike for themselves.)
v.s: What is [wrong] with you? How do you make judgement?
v.c: What is the matter with you? How do you judge?

v.s: Then will you not be reminded?
v.c: Will you not then be mindful?

q: Or have you some clear proof
(authority for your beliefs, which compel you cling to them so adamantly)?
v.s: Or do you have a clear authority?
v.c: Or do you have ˹any˺ compelling proof?

v.s: Then produce your scripture, if you should be truthful.
v.c: Then bring ˹us˺ your scripture, if what you say is true!

q: between Allaah and the Jinn. The Jinn already know that
they will be among those brought forward
v.s: And they have made [i.e., claimed] between Him and the jinn a lineage, but the jinn have already known that they [who made such claims] will be brought [to punishment].
v.c: They have also established a ˹marital˺ relationship between Him and the jinn. Yet the jinn ˹themselves˺ know well that such people will certainly be brought ˹for punishment˺.

v.s: Exalted is God above what they describe,
v.c: Glorified is Allah far above what they claim!

q: Of course, the condition of Allaah's sincere bondsmen is different
(they do not hold these fallacious beliefs but worship Allaah only).
v.s: Except the chosen servants of God [who do not share in that sin].
v.c: But not the chosen servants of Allah.

v.s: So indeed, you [disbelievers] and whatever you worship,
v.c: Surely you ˹pagans˺ and whatever ˹idols˺ you worship

v.s: You cannot tempt [anyone] away from Him
v.c: can never lure ˹anyone˺ away from Him

q: (he will turn away from Allaah regardless of the efforts of the Mushrikeen).
v.s: Except he who is to [enter and] burn in the Hellfire.
v.c: except those ˹destined˺ to burn in Hell.

q: The position of each of us
(It is in these fixed positions that the angels engage in Ibaadah all the time.)
v.s: [The angels say], "There is not among us any except that he has a known position.
v.c: ˹The angels respond,˺ “There is not one of us without an assigned station ˹of worship˺.

q: Indeed, we are standing in rows
v.s: And indeed, we are those who line up [for prayer].
v.c: We are indeed the ones lined up in ranks ˹for Allah˺.

v.s: And indeed, we are those who exalt God."
v.c: And we are indeed the ones ˹constantly˺ glorifying ˹His praise˺.”

q: It is a fact that these people
v.s: And indeed, they [i.e., the disbelievers] used to say,
v.c: They certainly used to say,

q: from the people of the past...”
v.s: "If we had a message from [those of] the former peoples,
v.c: “If only we had a Reminder like ˹those of˺ earlier peoples,

q: “...we would then surely have been Allaah's sincere
(by practising the injunctions of the scripture).'
v.s: We would have been the chosen servants of God."
v.c: we would have truly been Allah’s devoted servants.”

q: (the Qur'aan, which has come to them).
They will soon come to know
(the error of their ways when they face Allaah's punishment).
v.s: But they disbelieved in it, so they are going to know.
v.c: But ˹now˺ they reject it, so they will soon know.

q: has been issued concerning those of Our slaves who have been sent
v.s: And Our word [i.e., decree] has already preceded for Our servants, the messengers,
v.c: Our Word has already gone forth to Our servants, the messengers,

v.s: [That] indeed, they would be those given victory
v.c: that they would surely be helped,

v.s: And [that] indeed, Our soldiers [i.e., the believers] will be those who overcome.
v.c: and that Our forces will certainly prevail.

q: (and do not bother with their insults and taunts).
v.s: So, [O Muhammad], leave them for a time.
v.c: So turn away from the deniers for a while ˹O Prophet˺.

q: them, for they shall soon see
v.s: And see [what will befall] them, for they are going to see.
v.c: You will see ˹what will happen to˺ them, and they too will see!

q: Do they seek to hasten Our punishment?
v.s: Then for Our punishment are they impatient?
v.c: Do they ˹really˺ wish to hasten Our punishment?

q: then the morning of those who were warned
(because they will) all be destroyed in the punishment).
v.s: But when it descends in their territory, then evil is the morning of those who were warned.
v.c: Yet when it descends upon them: how evil will that morning be for those who had been warned!

q: (until the command of Jihaad is given).
v.s: And leave them for a time.
v.c: And turn away from them for a while.

v.s: And see, for they are going to see.
v.c: You will see, and they too will see!

q: Your Rabb, the Rabb of all honour is Pure
v.s: Exalted is your Lord, the Lord of might, above what they describe.
v.c: Glorified is your Lord—the Lord of Honour and Power—above what they claim!

v.s: And peace upon the messengers.
v.c: Peace be upon the messengers.

q: And all praise belongs to Allaah, the Rabb of the universe.
v.s: And praise to God, Lord of the worlds.
v.c: And praise be to Allah —Lord of all worlds.
